column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The commanders belong to the people in Hebrew, rather than explicitly to troops.
The Hebrew calls them His people rather than troops.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew lists the count of Judah with “and”, and repeats “men drawing the sword”; it does not explicitly say “including”.
The Hebrew does not explicitly repeat Joab’s name at the start of the verse.
The Hebrew calls this a matter, without explicitly naming a command.

The three alternatives are pictured as being stretched out over David.
The Hebrew says “take for yourself”.
The enemies’ sword is singular in Hebrew.
The human hand is singular in Hebrew.
Death is pictured as falling, without an explicit word “dead”.
The Hebrew does not explicitly add “the people” to the destroying angel’s activity.
The Hebrew orders the location as between earth and heaven.
The Hebrew emphatically repeats the verb stem for doing evil; it asks that the hand not be on the people for a plague, without an explicit “remain”.
